positions.commentary: The speaker notes that the Walton family was the only one to hold Walmart stock for the entire 50 years because it was a great business doing well.
The speaker describes IBM as a shadow of its former self and notes that investing in it hasn't been a pleasant exercise for a couple of decades.
The speaker questions whether Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, or Microsoft will still be thriving 20 or 40 years from now, stating he doesn't know if he would make a bet on them.

thesis: This episode argues that while certain legacy businesses like Walmart and Anheuser-Busch are fundamentally strong, they have not necessarily been great investments over the past several decades. The speaker questions the long-term viability of major tech giants like Apple and Microsoft, suggesting that even great businesses may not be suitable for long-term bets.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that the Walton family was the only one to hold Walmart stock for the entire 50 years because it was a great business doing well.
claims.quote: Nobody held Walmart stock for the entire 50 years, except the Walton family. And so here was a great business. It was obvious. It was a great business. It was doing well.

claims.claim: The speaker describes IBM as a shadow of its former self and notes that investing in it hasn't been a pleasant exercise for a couple of decades.
claims.quote: And now it's a shadow of its former self. And investing in IBM hasn't been a pleasant exercise for maybe a couple of decades now.

claims.claim: The speaker questions whether Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, or Microsoft will still be thriving 20 or 40 years from now, stating he doesn't know if he would make a bet on them.
claims.quote: Which of these will be with us 20 years from now, still thriving, 60 years from now. I don't know if I would make a bet that any of them will be thriving 40 years ago.

claims.quote: You mentioned tobacco. You mentioned beverage companies or alcoholic beverage companies. But when you look at a company at Anheuser-Busch or BTI, they've pretty much done they haven't performed very much, I would say, over the past several years.
